data.name: Kamadeva
data.gender_notes: Kamadeva is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kamadeva is the god of love, desire, and passion. He is depicted as an attractive man wielding a bow made of sugarcane and flowers, and an arrow tipped with the nectar of love. When he shoots this arrow at someone, they are overwhelmed with desire and fall in love. The name Kamadeva carries the meaning “God of love and desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kamadeva usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of love and attraction in the universe
data.etymology: Kamadeva belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of love and desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kamadeva total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Kamadeva is a significant figure in Hindu art and literature. He is often portrayed in temple carvings and murals, and his story is told through various mythological texts. He is believed to trigger the feelings of love, attraction, and romance in people, and is often invoked during weddings and other celebratory events to ensure the presence of love and passion.
data.spiritual_significance: Kamadeva represents the emotional and passionate side of human nature. He symbolizes the power of love and desire in our lives, and how they can bring us joy, happiness, and even spiritual growth. In Hindu philosophy, the harmony between the physical and emotional aspects of our being is essential for spiritual evolution. Kamadeva reminds us to acknowledge and honor our feelings, and to use them to foster deep connections with others and with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kamadeva, the Hindu God of Desire and Passion, embodies the intoxicating allure of love and the impulse to create new life. His arrow, tipped with the fragrant flower of love, pierces the hearts of mortals, igniting the flame of passion and inspiring the creation of new bonds.

historical_references.reference: Kamadeva is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, where he is described as the god of desire and love. He is depicted as having the power to arouse desire in the hearts of gods and men.

Kamadeva is also mentioned in the Puranic literature, where he is described as the son of Lord Vishnu and Goddess Rati. He is said to have a powerful arrow, the 'Mohana Shakti', which can make even the most devout ascetics fall into deep desire and lust.

modern_usage.modern_context: Kamadeva, also known as the God of Love or the God of Desire in Hindu mythology, is a popular deity in Indian culture. His iconography often depicts him as an attractive man carrying a bow and arrow, which he uses to shoot arrows of love into the hearts of gods and mortals, causing them to fall in love. In modern contexts, Kamadeva is often referred to as 'Cupid' in Western culture. He is a significant figure in Hindu mythology and continues to be celebrated in various Indian cultural festivals. In the digital age, Kamadeva's image has been adopted and popularized on social media platforms, where he is often depicted as a symbol of romantic love and desire. #Kamadev #HinduMythology #Love
